prompts.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: literary fantasy short-story cover, portrait 9:16, requested 864x1536 pixels. Create a novel cover, visually inviting, warm comic affection with dignity.
Visual references: attached images 1 and 2 are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY from the collection. Match their broad rhythmic value/color shapes, varied directional opaque oil strokes, connected dark passages, selective impasto, simplified architecture, natural motivated light. Do not copy their scenery. Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil painting, no glossy faces or uniform embossed strokes.
Scene: the threshold of a tall timber adventurers' guild. Looking into firelit long tables, timber beams and a notices-covered wall, daytime outside. A few simplified guild patrons have stopped to look, no crowd conversion. Four adult fantasy adventurers enter as a loose group. Focus on a small earnest goblin paladin at front, facing inward in a proud three-quarter profile with chin up. His friends have warm messy overlapping silhouettes behind him, all distinct and readable.
Sir Tallow: roughly three feet tall, olive-green skin, large pointed ears, adult face with long pointed nose, amber eyes, no facial hair. Battered but freshly polished fitted steel breastplate and helmet with ears accommodated. Long claret cape nearly to heels, sword at left hip; small steel shield on right engraved with an oil-lamp emblem and tiny silver flame (emblem, NOT actual fire). Faith and earnest courage, not sinister monster.
Vorrick: tall broad adult orc with tusks, blue scholar's robes, carefully holding a book bound in pale calfskin. Laureth: slender adult female elf with fine cheekbones, practical moss-brown travel clothes, a long-hafted axe slung over shoulder with a berry-stained tassel (not blood), dry amused expression. Harn: immense adult Goliath, gray stone-toned skin, bald, restrained dark leather/cloth clothes with sleeves, enormous gentle hands; bends subtly beneath lintel, quiet observant rogue, no bulk plate armor. Their relative heights must be coherent.
Composition: monumental door uprights frame a tiny armored leading figure, friends stacked behind and up into the interior. Painted dark negative space at upper third supports clear elegant cream serif title. No illustrated plot summary or instructional diagram. Exact title text rendered ONCE as part of painting: "An Opening". No author name, subtitle or other readable writing. No modern objects, extra limbs, duplicate characters, dramatic rim lighting, automatic orange-blue contrast. Keep characters non-graphic and fully clothed.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset: landscape character reference sheet, requested 1536x1024 pixels. Exact readable heading "Sir Tallow", and beneath it the exact story title "An Opening", each once. Character and costume sheet for future illustrators, NOT scene portrait.
Image 1 is accepted story cover and is an IDENTITY/COSTUME REFERENCE for the small goblin in the foreground only. Preserve his olive-green skin, amber eyes, huge pointed ears, long pointed adult nose, friendly earnest adult face, no beard, petite solid build, the same steel armor pieces, ear-accommodating helmet, claret cape, boots and silver oil-lamp shield emblem. Do not depict the other cover characters. Image 2 is a FORMAT reference only from another story; do not borrow that human identity or costume. Image 3 is oil-painting STYLE reference.
Layout on light warm neutral painted ground: three coherent full-body views of Sir Tallow in arrival costume (front three-quarter, side, back), one full-body departure version with armor removed, two close face/expression studies (hopeful composure and worried concentration), and a small clean prop grouping if space. Keep every view recognizably the same character, proportions and clothes; both legs and hands anatomically coherent.
Arrival costume: polished battered breastplate and articulated steel plate, little steel helmet with ear clearance, long claret cape to near heels, sword sheathed at LEFT hip, shield at RIGHT arm engraved with an oil lamp and tiny silver flame (not fire). The emblem must be consistent across views.
Departure costume: no breastplate, helmet or shield worn. A quilted brown-beige tunic with black-thread patch at ONE elbow, travel trousers and boots, same sword still sheathed at left hip, claret cape tucked through belt clear of knees. At right side a small belt pouch containing one slender curved-tip latch tool. Props if shown: the lamp shield and helmet titled "Pledged gear", a delicate curved-tip latch tool titled "Harn's tool". Labels to views: "Arrival", "Departure", "Hopeful", "Concentrating". Minimal labels, legible exact spelling.
Art: broad rhythmic opaque oil strokes, warm cream background, restrained connected shadows and selective impasto, collection Group of Seven inspired treatment matched to cover. Clear readable silhouettes rather than glossy photorealism or fuzzy ornate clutter. No extra characters, inappropriate skin exposure, halos, magic fire, author text, duplicated titles. Artwork must be practical model reference and still painterly.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset: location reference oil painting for "An Opening", landscape 1536x1024 pixels. An adventurers' guild hall on a clear morning, seen from just inside its tall open timber entrance looking toward the registry counter and long tables. Location reference, not plot summary, no text overlay.
Attached images 1 and 2 are collection STYLE references only, not scenery to reproduce. Use Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil: broad rhythmic value and color masses, varied directional opaque strokes, selective thick impasto, connected dark passages and lost edges, simplified architecture, motivated firelight and daylight; not glossy rendered interior.
Finished prose facts: heavy tall wooden entry doors with simple reachable latch; firelight; long communal tables; timber roof beams; very many parchment adventure notices nailed on walls (no legible writing). A registry counter with ledger, quill, small folder and map, lockable drawers. A separate equipment desk nearby has a CLOSED tall lockable wooden cupboard behind it, containing pledged gear; small sound rope coil and covered lantern nearby. Need enough open space by registry for two chairs to support an axe haft during a small rehearsal. Keep a cozy tavern-like guild atmosphere, realistic scale and usable circulation, no palace throne or ornate cathedral. A few chairs and benches, modest fire hearth, daylight stripe from door. Painting is unpeopled so later artists can locate scenes.
Composition: near dark timber doorway frames space; long tables lead toward registrar desk; equipment counter and its closed cupboard readable as a distinct nook on one side. Warm gray, earth, muted russet, restrained gold cream motivated light with connected shadows. Architectural perspective coherent; ceiling beams high enough that an eight-foot Goliath just approaches one, entrance requires him to duck. No sewers, pipes, battle aftermath, dead bodies, fortress crawlway, water machinery, magical glowing lights, diagrams, readable signage, border, title, modern objects.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the attached location oil painting with ONE local correction: replace the two tall narrow backless stools in front of the distant registry counter (near image center) with two modest sturdy freestanding wooden CHAIRS, each with a low visible back and broad seat. The chairs should be close enough to one another to support an axe haft across their seats for a small goblin's practice, with an accessible gap and sensible floor perspective. Keep their scale ordinary, not giant.
Preserve the painting's architecture, near doorway, firelight, sun stripe, notices, registry counter with map and ledger, distinct equipment desk and closed cupboard on right, lantern/rope, all tables, banners, palette and expressive opaque oil strokes. Do not add people, an axe, text, extra clutter or glowing magic. Only change those two seats. Keep landscape 1536x1024 and the same Group of Seven inspired painted treatment.
